data.narrative:
Hexium is a Seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Charlie Jarrott and Jacob Peterson that has raised $10M+. The valuation assessment draws on a nuclear energy comparable universe of 11 peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Nano Nuclear Energy, Oklo, X-Energy, Fuse Energy, and Applied Atomics.

Stage-progression analysis, the only methodologically sound approach given data constraints, applies a 2.5x multiplier to the $10M total raised proxy, yielding a $25M implied valuation. This multiplier reflects typical step-up dynamics from Seed to Series A in the frontier nuclear sector. Peer-median triangulation was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow nuclear energy peer set; expanding to all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable measurement error.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $21M to $29M, with a median of $25M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single robust method rather than convergence across multiple approaches. Key uncertainties include the absence of recent transaction data for narrowly-staged nuclear peers and limited visibility into burn rate and runway relative to the $10M raised. The range assumes typical Seed dynamics; material deviations in capital efficiency or regulatory trajectory could shift outcomes materially.
